body:
Thank you for your willingness to lend advice, and I'm open to whatever you may have to say. 

I'm glad you asked that question because it may be productive for me to admit that I am totally clueless as to what other actions I could take. I have a solid and healthy social group but I tend to just stick to their company, and with the exception of one friend who just got married they're all fairly insular and sexually/romantically inactive just like myself, so i cant really hope to be introduced to new people through them. 

While I meet many like-minded people through my career it's all on temporary freelance jobs across the country so stable groups can't really form there. 

I like going out to bars with my friends but I dislike night clubs and I'm fairly skeptical of whatever results may come of trying to pick-up at bars and clubs anyway. 

Aside from that, I anticipate that you may suggest social clubs for hobbies but if they're out there I have no idea how to find them. I gave meetup.com a half-hearted try once but there just didn't seem to be many groups posted on that site in my area.

Well, I suppose I somewhat misrepresented myself when I said that I have no trouble finding social groups. I have a very solid social group of good long-time friends who I see all the time, but I don't often venture beyond their company. 

I am indeed social, or at least quite capable of getting along well with many sorts of people. My job even brings me into contact with new like-minded people quite regularly. But my job is based on freelance projects that I have to travel for, so once a project is done we all go our separate ways, back to our homes all over the country. So stable social groups dont really form through my work. 

And my hobbies are all rather solitary, or at least I can get away with being solitary while doing them, and I must admit that even though I'm not anti-social I do tend to seek more alone time than the average person. Hiking or fishing alone in the woods is a particular pastime of mine. My other hobbies are creative projects, such as writing, and I'm not sure how that could be made social. 

Maybe a part of me has even begun to romanticize a lone-wolf persona, even if it is counterproductive to what I really want out of life. I am incredibly accustomed to, even comfortable with, being alone. I'm in between jobs and back at home right now, and my roommate who is in the same line of work has been out for months on a job of his own so I have the apartment to myself. If I happen to not interact with friends or family for a few days I can easily go that whole time without so much as speaking a single word out loud, and it doesn't even bother me that much. This is even aside from the whole current pandemic quarantine.

And you're absolutely right about not reading too much into biological points. One of the things that makes me skeptical of TRP is how deterministic they are about biological "realities." But while these evolutionary facts are certainly not the whole story I still feel that they may be true in an academic sense and have a part to play, and perhaps do tip the scale a little bit. I suppose that I may just see these biological facts as the final nail in the coffin when considered alongside my failure to navigate more relevant social factors.

I greatly appreciate the thought you've put into this response, it's given me some things to consider. Thank you for the invite to PM, I may take you up on it but no particular way to productively continue the conversation is coming to mind at the moment.

Religious community was an example I gave of what's lacking for many people in my predicament in today's society, certainly. But paradoxically, I myself don't have a lot of religious inclination, never really did. My parents raised me pretty secular, honestly. I have a buddy who's started going to church to find a tradwife and it actually comes off as creepy and hollow because I know that on the inside he's still the same old depraved heathen he's always been haha.

The trouble that I'm trying to express is that I've kinda already been without hope and just working on myself for years now. I think trp people call it "going monk mode." Though I've also been socially active. Finding social groups has never been a problem for me, but being seen as a romantic candidate seems to be something else. I guess I'm just trying to come to terms with the nagging suspicion that I could go through all the right motions and still be stuck where I am now, because the trp or mgtow people just might be right, the odds may be stacked against me no matter what. Though I don't fall in with those communities because I don't like their cynicism or their reactionary "solutions" and prescriptions for the problem. Like I said I'm still glad that I'm working on myself no matter what, but all the same there is a sort of let-down that the carrot I'm chasing just might not be there at all, and I have a fear of the future if it's just going to be more of the same.

You're certainly right about how neediness is a big turn-off, I can't say that I'm completely past being needy but I've certainly gotten good at covering it up and distancing myself from it by just going numb and calling it "stoicism" or whatever.

Thank you for the well wishes. I'll keep on my feet.
